questions.title: Mycoplasma resistant to penicillin
questions.question: Mycoplasmas are bacterial cells that?

options.A: Fail to reproduce on artificial media

explanations.A: Incorrect. Mycoplasma can be cultured on enriched artificial (cell-free) media, unlike obligate intracellular bacteria such as Chlamydia or Rickettsia.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mycoplasma is genetically incapable of synthesising peptidoglycan and so permanently lacks a rigid cell wall -- its pleomorphic shape is a direct consequence.
explanations.C: Correct. Penicillin and other beta-lactams work by blocking peptidoglycan cross-linking in the bacterial cell wall. Mycoplasma has no peptidoglycan wall at all, so it has no target for the drug. It is therefore intrinsically resistant to penicillin, not by an acquired mechanism but simply because the drug's target is absent.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Gram staining depends on differential retention of crystal violet by a peptidoglycan cell wall -- with no cell wall, Mycoplasma does not stain reliably by Gram's method.

questions.learning_objective: State that Mycoplasma is intrinsically resistant to penicillin because it has no peptidoglycan cell wall to target.

questions.title: Fungal cell wall major components
questions.question: Which statement regarding fungal cell walls is correct?

options.A: Major components are proteins as chitin, glucan, mannans
options.B: Cell wall is not essential for fungal viability of survival
options.C: Ligands associated with cell wall mediate attachment to host cells
options.D: Cell wall components are the targets for the major classes of antifungal drugs as polyenes and azoles
options.E: Cell wall components rarely stimulate immune response

explanations.A: Correct. The medically important fungi have a cell wall whose major components are chitin, glucan and mannan (mannoproteins). This is a mixture of structural polysaccharides and glycoproteins. It is chemically and structurally distinct from bacterial peptidoglycan, the basis of the bacterial cell wall.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The fungal cell wall is essential for viability -- it maintains cell shape and osmotic integrity, and disrupting it (as echinocandin antifungals do) is lethal to the fungus.
explanations.C: Incorrect (in this context). While cell-wall-associated ligands can mediate host attachment for some fungi, the question is asking for the wall's actual chemical composition, which A names directly.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Polyenes and azoles target the fungal cell MEMBRANE (ergosterol), not the cell wall -- echinocandins are the antifungal class that targets the cell wall (beta-glucan synthase), so this option misattributes the wall as the target of the wrong drug classes.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Fungal cell wall components (such as beta-glucan and mannan) are recognized by host pattern-recognition receptors and do stimulate an immune response -- they do not "rarely" do so.

questions.learning_objective: State that chitin, glucan and mannan are the major components of the fungal cell wall.

questions.title: Chitin is a component of fungal cell wall
questions.question: Which of the following is a component of fungal cell wall?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Teichoic acid is a component of the Gram-positive bacterial cell wall, not the fungal cell wall.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lipopolysaccharide is a component of the Gram-negative bacterial outer membrane, not the fungal cell wall.
explanations.C: Correct. Chitin is a structural polysaccharide that is the main component of most fungal cell walls. It sits alongside glucan and mannan as the wall's other major components. All three are chemically and structurally distinct from either the Gram-positive or the Gram-negative bacterial cell wall.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Since teichoic acid and lipopolysaccharide are both bacterial (not fungal) wall components, "all of these" is wrong -- only chitin among the listed options is fungal.

questions.learning_objective: Identify chitin as a component of the fungal cell wall, distinct from bacterial wall components.

questions.title: Fungi with true mycelium are filamentous fungi
questions.question: Fungi with true mycelium are called?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Yeasts are unicellular, budding fungi that do not form a true mycelium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Yeast-like fungi (such as Candida) form pseudohyphae, not a true, continuously branching mycelium.
explanations.C: Correct. Fungi that grow with a true mycelium -- a mass of branching, thread-like hyphae -- are filamentous fungi, i.e. molds, in contrast to the unicellular yeasts and the intermediate yeast-like or dimorphic forms.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Filamentous fungi" is the standard correct term, so "none of these" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: Identify filamentous fungi (molds) as those growing with a true mycelium.

questions.title: Dimorphic fungi show both yeast and filamentous forms
questions.question: Fungi showing yeast form as well as filamentous form are called?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A pure yeast grows only as a unicellular budding form, never switching to a filamentous form.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Yeast-like fungi form pseudohyphae but do not undergo a temperature-dependent switch between a true mold form and a true yeast form.
explanations.C: Correct. Dimorphic fungi grow as a mold (filamentous, hyphal) form in the environment, at room temperature. They convert to a yeast form in vivo, at body temperature (37 C). Possessing both growth forms depending on conditions is exactly what "dimorphic" means.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Molds grow only in the filamentous form and do not switch to a yeast form.

questions.learning_objective: Identify dimorphic fungi as those showing both a yeast and a filamentous form.

questions.title: Mycelium is a collection of intertwined hyphae
questions.question: Collection of intertwined hyphae is called?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Conidia are asexual fungal spores, a reproductive structure, not a mass of hyphae.
explanations.B: Correct. Individual fungal hyphae can aggregate into an intertwined, visible mass. The resulting macroscopic structure is called the mycelium. This is distinct from a single hypha, a yeast colony, or fungal spores, each of which is a separate structural concept.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Flagella are motility organelles (as in zoospores), unrelated to hyphal aggregation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pseudohyphae are chains of elongated budding yeast cells, not a mass of true hyphae.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Budding cells describes the reproductive process of yeasts, not a collection of hyphae.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the mycelium as the macroscopic aggregation of fungal hyphae.

questions.title: Fungal cell wall composed of chitin
questions.question: Cell wall of fungus is composed of?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Peptidoglycan is a bacterial cell wall component, chemically and structurally distinct from the fungal wall.
explanations.B: Correct. Chitin is the main structural polysaccharide composing most fungal cell walls. It sits alongside glucan and mannan as the wall's other major components. Together these give the fungal wall its rigidity, distinct in chemistry from any bacterial wall.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mannitol is a sugar alcohol, not a structural fungal cell wall component (mannan, a related polysaccharide, is a wall component, but mannitol is not the same molecule).
explanations.D: Incorrect. Casein is a milk protein, unrelated to fungal cell wall structure.

questions.learning_objective: State that the fungal cell wall is composed of chitin.

questions.title: Morphological classification of Candida is yeast
questions.question: The morphological classification of candida is?

explanations.A: Incorrect (for this bank's teaching level). Candida is taught here alongside Cryptococcus neoformans as a yeast example, not grouped with the classic thermally dimorphic fungi (such as Histoplasma) that switch between a mold form in the environment and a yeast form in vivo.
explanations.B: Correct. Candida is presented as a yeast in the governed teaching used by this bank. Cryptococcus neoformans is offered alongside it as the other yeast example. Neither is classed here as a mold or a classic thermally dimorphic fungus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Molds/filamentous fungi grow as true, branching hyphae -- Candida is a budding yeast (forming pseudohyphae in tissue, not true hyphae).
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Yeast" is the correct classification, so "none of the above" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: Classify Candida morphologically as a yeast.
